mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Employment growth was 137,846 thousand persons as of 2008-04-15
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.0% signals a weakening labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances (UNRATE > 5.0), or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a contraction in both the housing sector and manufacturing, which reduces overall economic activity and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Housing starts were 1065.0 thousand units and industrial production was 111.9137 as of 2008-04-15
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and INDPRO decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS above 3.0% and rising), the increased cost of capital reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 3.0 and rising, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS increases, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
